messages:
ingrid: alert — sfo-dedicated pool GPU alloc at 98% across gpu-pool-12, queue latencies spiking, some tenant requests returning 503s. provisioning reports AZ capacity issues. tagging for response.
charlie: seeing large burst from a batch job tenant, queue depth x15 normal. can we avoid full failover? prefer spilling low-priority first.
maria: suggest gradual traffic shift: low-priority orgs -> hosted. plan: set routing policy weights +10% to hosted every 90s, evaluate errors/latency. I'll run the upgrade.
alex: +1. keep enterprise customers pinned to dedicated (pin list in config). also enable model-variant fallback so we serve quantized hosted models for non-SLA orgs to save cost/latency.
devops-bot: autoscaler: scale-up triggered for sfo-dedicated (requested +2 nodes). cloud provider ETA 7m due to AZ stock. current nodes provisioning: 0/2.
sre-lead: start throttling non-SLA traffic at 0.5 rps/org to reduce burst while weights shift. Will post when done.
charlie: applied throttles, confirmed via /api/metrics -> per-org qps dropped ~60% for low tier. queue length stabilizing.
maria: starting weight shift now. command: ```POST /routing/update {"region":"sfo","policy":"weight","delta_hosted":10}``` doing 10% -> 20% -> 30% over 5m.
ingrid: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/sfo-pool shows gpu_util and queued_requests. keeping eye on OOM logs.
charlie: noticed worker-3 OOMs on init for model 'redwood-v2-small'. restarting the pod now, tailing logs.
alex: on config side I pushed a transient route that maps redwood-v2-small -> redwood-v2-small-quantized-hosted for non-sla. snippet:
```
routes:
  - match: {model: "redwood-v2-small", org_tier: "non-sla"}
    action: {target: "hosted", variant:"quantized"}
```
will roll back after pressure subsides.
maria: weight shift at 30% now. errors marginally up for one org (org-42) — they have higher concurrency, increasing their hosted slots temporarily.
sre-lead: finance FYI — hosted fallback increases unit cost est ~1.7x for routed tokens. notifying finance channel.
ingrid: updates: autoscaler reported nodes up (2/2) but kube-scheduler hasn't placed new pods yet; there are still pending pods due to GPU plugin bug. I'm opening a quick follow-up ticket.
charlie: hotfix: kube-plugin restart cleared scheduling. new pods booting, health checks passing.
alex: once dedicated pool stabilizes we'll ramp weights down. proposed rollback plan: reduce hosted weight by 15% every 90s starting 10m after node readiness and monitoring error rate <0.5% for 5m.
ingrid: summary: 1) throttles applied to non-SLA 2) progressive weight shift to hosted (30%) 3) model-variant fallback for non-SLA 4) autoscaler + kube-plugin fix brought nodes 5) rollback plan ready. keeping this thread open for 30m, will post final closure.
maria: thanks all. :thumbsup:
devops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0411-SFO-CAPACITY. Link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-2026-0411
sre-lead: closing ops loop: observed queue and error metrics returning to baseline after rolling back weights to 10%. follow-up action: file a postmortem for GPU plugin scheduling + improve autoscaler backoff.
ingrid: closing — moving to postmortem thread.
